newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan backs Sierra Leone's ouster by Commonwealth.
newsitem.headline: Annan backs Sierra Leone's ouster by Commonwealth.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan backed a decision by the Commonwealth on Friday to suspend Sierra Leone until the military junta that seized power in May is replaced by a democratically elected government.
Asked for comment on the action of Commonwealth ministers at a meeting in London, Annan replied: "The Commonwealth, like all law-respecting institutions, has been determined to restore democracy.

"I hope the coup-makers in Sierra Leone will really begin to understand that the international community is not accepting what they have done and that perhaps they should begin to rethink ... and step down."

He was speaking to reporters after attending a brief meeting of the Security Council at which Nigeria's foreign minister, Chief Tom Ikimi, gave details of an initiative by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to restore democracy to Sierra Leone, where civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah was toppled seven weeks ago by Major Johnny Paul Koromah.

At a meeting in Conakry, Guinea, June 26, ECOWAS foreign ministers said no country should recognise the rebel regime and pledged to work toward the reinstatement of the legitimate government through dialogue, sanctions and an embargo, and if necessary the use of force.
They set up a four-nation committee, comprising the foreign ministers of Nigeria, Guinea, Ivory Coast and Ghana.
Ikimi said the people of Sierra Leone, ECOWAS and the entire African continent looked forward to the support of the Security Council.

"That support, we hope, should be a clear and unequivocal message to the regime in Sierra Leone to comply with the demands of the international community and return power to the legitimate government of President Tejan Kabbah."
The only other speaker was ambassador Machivenyika Mapuranga of Zimbabwe, whose country holds the chairmanship of the Organisation of African Unity, which has also condemned the Sierra Leone coup.
The council was expected to issue a statement later calling for the restoration of democracy in that country.
